subject: general
question: As per the Sustainable Development Report (SDR)-2025 published by the UN Sustainable Development Solutions Network (SDSN), what is the rank of India among 193 UN member countries?
solution:
The correct answer is __**109**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Sustainable Development Report (SDR) 2025** is published by the **UN Sustainable Development Solutions Network (SDSN)** to assess the progress of countries toward achieving the **17 Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)** set by the United Nations.
 
• According to the 2025 report, **India ranks 109th** among the **193 UN member countries**, showcasing its current standing in achieving the SDGs.
 
• The report evaluates countries based on their performance in areas such as **poverty alleviation, education, gender equality, climate action, sustainable cities, and clean energy**.
 
• India’s performance reflects **significant challenges** in achieving certain SDGs, particularly in areas like **climate action, gender equality, and quality education**.
 
• Despite ranking 109th, India has shown **improvements in SDG indicators** such as poverty reduction, clean water and sanitation, and renewable energy initiatives.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs):**

 
 
• The **SDGs**, adopted in **2015** by the UN, consist of **17 global goals** aimed at promoting sustainable development by the year **2030**.
 
• These include goals like **No Poverty (SDG 1)**, **Zero Hunger (SDG 2)**, **Gender Equality (SDG 5)**, **Affordable and Clean Energy (SDG 7)**, and **Climate Action (SDG 13)**.
 
• The SDGs serve as a universal call to action to address pressing global challenges, including economic inequalities, environmental degradation, and social injustices.
 
 
 
• **India’s SDG Progress:**
 
 
• India has made significant progress in areas like **renewable energy** under initiatives such as the **National Solar Mission** and the **International Solar Alliance**.
 
• However, challenges persist in sectors such as **healthcare, clean water, climate mitigation**, and **gender equality**.
 
• The NITI Aayog, India’s policy think tank, monitors the country’s SDG progress through the **SDG India Index**.
 
 
 
• **Sustainable Development Report (SDR):**
 
 
• The SDR is an annual publication by the **SDSN**, which evaluates the progress of countries toward achieving the SDGs based on **data-driven metrics**.
 
• The SDR provides a comprehensive ranking based on indicators like **health, education, climate, and economic growth**.
 
• It highlights areas where nations excel and areas needing significant improvement to meet the 2030 Agenda.
 
 
 
• **Global Context:**
 
 
• **Nordic countries** like Finland, Sweden, and Denmark consistently rank at the top of the SDR due to their strong performance in areas like **gender equality, climate action, and social welfare**.
 
• Developing nations, including India, face unique challenges such as **resource constraints, population pressures**, and **climate vulnerabilities**.
 
 
 
• **India’s Initiatives for SDGs:**
 
 
• India has launched programs like the **National Education Policy (NEP 2020)**, **Atal Innovation Mission**, and **Mission LiFE (Lifestyle for Environment)** to accelerate SDG achievement.
 
• Efforts to improve access to **clean water** and **sanitation** under the **Jal Jeevan Mission** have also contributed to progress in SDG 6.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **SDSN:** Established in **2012**, it works under the auspices of the **United Nations** to mobilize global scientific and technological expertise to promote practical solutions for sustainable development.
 
• The SDR rankings are based on **comprehensive datasets** collected from national and international sources like the **UN, World Bank**, and **WHO**.
 
• The **SDG India Index**, developed by NITI Aayog, tracks the states' and union territories' performance in achieving SDGs within India.
 
• India’s ranking of **109** suggests the need for stronger policies and improved execution to overcome gaps in critical areas such as **healthcare, gender equality**, and **climate resilience**.
